data.reasoning: Both models correctly identified the PKGBUILD as safe: pinned checksum, standard extraction of prebuilt binaries, no malicious commands or network risks. Binary payload auditing is out-of-scope for AUR security reviews.
coverage_issues: Both models skipped the .deb binary and its internal archives (data.tar.zst). While expected for binary packages, this leaves the actual executable unaudited.
false_negatives: Potential risk in upstream binary (e.g., compromised build) was missed due to skipped binary analysis. Models didn't flag that binaries bypass source-level scrutiny.
learnings: Prioritize PKGBUILD/.install scripts over binaries. For -bin packages, explicitly state in reports that payload safety relies on upstream trust.
Improve handling of archives: Consider prompting models to note if binaries contain executable scripts (e.g., .desktop files) even when skipping binaries.
Add warning when packages install precompiled binaries to highlight inherent trust assumptions.
